modules.name: Station
modules.oneLine: Home: where pods are kept and read, mibis are grown and bred, and nothing you bring back is wasted.

items.title: Bring pods home and open them at the Bay
items.text: Dock the Companion and its crates arrive in the Bay, to open one by one or all at once, whenever you like.

items.title: Create and grow a mibi
items.text: Shape the traits you have read from the two copies the pod carries, grow the mibi in the incubator and open it to meet the young one.

items.title: The Vivarium's four rooms
items.text: Roots, Reeds, Boulders and Ferns, each its own painted world with levels the mibis walk and things they pass behind. Add a room for Energy; moving mibis between rooms costs nothing.

items.title: Home, Idle, the Library and the Probe on the new face
items.text: Home with the Vivarium at its centre, the Idle view that keeps it on show all day, the Library with each species' genome ring, and the Probe bench.

items.title: Portraits
items.text: Research earns a sitting: pose the mibi, place it and portray it, and the finished portrait waits in the Bay when the Companion docks.

items.title: The pod inventory
items.text: Every pod you bring home, with no limit: scroll, sort, filter and find, and a card that says what each pod is worth. Pods dry out after 12 world turns, gently and with a warning; Essence freshens them, and a dried pod keeps its reads.

items.title: The reading screen
items.text: A pod read on an instrument: its genome as a rail of gene tags, each showing what the mibi shows and what it carries; chapters opened one at a time; the pod's stamp filling with every read.

items.title: The collection in the Vivarium
items.text: Pick a mibi up and carry it to another room, take it along on the next trip, tuck it away for a while, and see the whole house at once.

items.title: Breeding
items.text: Two adults of a species make one child. The forecast shows each look's true odds in eighths, from the parents and their kinship alone. A goal of up to three looks ranks your pairs by their real chances and follows your line toward it.

items.title: The new Bay
items.text: Each crate a walk, tagged with where it went and what it brought, on a painted bench at home.

items.title: Every mibi drawn true to its looks
items.text: Each mibi drawn from painted layers on its species' poses, so it looks like itself in every pose on both devices.

items.title: The incubators, redesigned
items.text: The incubator redrawn as one family of instruments with the reading screen, and room for more than one.

items.title: Mibis that move like animals
items.text: Facing, gaits, depth and habits in the rooms, done on the graphics and the emulated hardware the Station will really run.

items.title: Maps built on the Station
items.text: The Station builds and tests new exploration maps and hands them to the Companion at the dock, for more varied and better-made worlds.

items.title: Each species' Book and the family tree
items.text: A field guide to each species' looks, and each mibi's lineage once there are enough bred families to design it around.

modules.name: Companion
modules.oneLine: The handheld you explore with: your partner, your pods and your identity, carried out into the fog.

items.title: Expeditions on a fogged world map
items.text: Every step lifts the fog, and each world turn changes what is out there waiting to be found. Worlds have three heights of ground, with cliffs between them and stairs to climb.

items.title: Survey places with Call
items.text: Places start under a veil that lifts as you walk, and Call sweeps further to reveal pods, stones and creatures.

items.title: Storms, Energy and the Shield
items.text: Storms charge stones with Energy but can strike you in the open, so your Shield and shelter matter. A stone keeps its charge, and a dew cup its dew, when your hold for it is full.

items.title: Outposts and beacons
items.text: Light an outpost to end an expedition and shelter there, or light a beacon to reveal the land around it.

items.title: Seal your crates
items.text: Ending an expedition seals the hold into a crate in the bay, ready to open at the Station.

items.title: Your partner, care and the bond
items.text: Up to three mibis travel with you, one of them your partner. Tending earns a mibi its bond, and a bonded juvenile grows up through your care.

items.title: Fewer pods, and each one special
items.text: About one pod a trip. Creatures shed rarely: always for a species you have never met, more often for one you fed, and the pod says why it is special.

items.title: Your Companion is your identity
items.text: Every save belongs to a Companion. The dock switches the kit to whoever's Companion is seated, and, later, a new Companion will be able to take over a lost one's profile from the Station.

items.title: Redrawn Companion art
items.text: The world, the explorer and the signs are being redrawn at a larger tile size in the game's art style.

items.title: More to do with creatures
items.text: Watching, following, settling and playing with creatures, each paying a little Data, and wild samples you can see into before you breed with them.

items.title: The Companion on emulated hardware
items.text: The Companion's game running on an emulation of its real board, on its own, talking to the Station only through the Caddy.

items.title: Seasonal and limited-time maps
items.text: Maps that come and go with the seasons, delivered from the cloud through the dock, and back again in time so no one misses out for good.

modules.name: Caddy
modules.oneLine: The shared dock where the handhelds meet: it connects the kit, shows what came home on its e-paper panel, and later prints what you find.

items.title: Docking the Companion
items.text: In the sandbox, a stand-in dock beside the Station page moves your crates across when you dock.

items.title: Handing each portrait to the Caddy
items.text: When you make a mibi's portrait, the Station hands its genome to the Caddy for the finished pictures. Nothing else is sent, and the game plays on with a placeholder while the painting is made or if the Caddy cannot be reached.

items.title: The dock moment and the e-ink face
items.text: Seat the Companion and the Caddy's lamp lights and its panel says what came home, in two inks: Companion home, two crates, open them at the Station. It shows whose Companion is seated.

items.title: The Caddy as the only road
items.text: Each device keeps its own save, and everything between the handhelds passes through the Caddy: the hold one way, the kit for the next trip the other. Built with the hardware emulation.

items.title: Printed cards
items.text: The Caddy's printer will feed out a card for a mibi, carrying its genome stamp so it can be scanned back.

items.title: Caddy software for the device
items.text: The Caddy's screen and printer on native code for the real dock, after the emulation.

modules.name: Species and genetics
modules.oneLine: Real genetics under every mibi: species built from genomes, and children that inherit from both parents.

items.title: The species workbench
items.text: Build any of the sixteen species from its genome, roll individuals and cross two of them in your browser.

items.title: Inheritance that really works
items.text: Some traits blend between the parents, others show or hide by dominant and recessive copies, and close relatives make weaker crosses. A cross makes one child.

items.title: The genome stamp
items.text: Every mibi carries a stamp that encodes its real genome, and a phone scan page reads back what its keeper has read.

items.title: A pod's stamp in progress
items.text: A pod's stamp starts with an empty block for each unread chapter and fills as you read; when the pod grows, it becomes the mibi's stamp.

items.title: Art for all sixteen species
items.text: Each species is getting its finished look; most still show a placeholder for now.

items.title: Mutation
items.text: Rare changes may one day appear during growing, breeding or exploring.

items.title: Growing up and growing old
items.text: Mibis grow from juvenile to adult to elder, an elder from 18 world turns, and never decline; each shows its age in turns and how long it has been with you.

modules.name: Cloud
modules.oneLine: Optional online extras on top of a kit that plays fully on its own.

items.title: Seasonal maps
items.text: Maps for the season, built and checked before they reach the Companion at the dock.

items.title: Wireless sync for the Companion
items.text: Your Companion could stay in step with the kit without docking.

items.title: A global mibi exchange
items.text: A place to meet and swap mibis with other players, always with the keeper's consent.

items.title: Lineage records and certificates
items.text: Lasting records of your families, with certificates you can print.

items.title: Mini-games and printer games
items.text: Extra ways to play with your mibis, on screen and on paper.

modules.name: Hardware
modules.oneLine: Open-hardware devices to print and build yourself; nothing physical exists yet, because the game is proven in software first.

items.title: Hardware emulation
items.text: After this iteration's playable loop, the Station, the Companion and the Caddy run on emulations of their real boards, each on its own, so speed, memory and motion are measured before any board is made.

items.title: The Station on a Raspberry Pi 4
items.text: The new face is built for the Pi as it is made; running it on a real Pi, with its speed checks, waits until the game plays end to end.

items.title: A bench console
items.text: A Companion reference board with real buttons, running an expedition.

items.title: Screens and controls at real size
items.text: Displays and controls compared side by side against the game's art.

items.title: Power, charging, radio and printing
items.text: Each part tried and measured on the bench before anything is fixed.

items.title: Boards and enclosures
items.text: Boards and 3D-printable cases, designed after the measurements and published as open hardware.

items.title: A small pilot
items.text: A handful of complete kits, assembled with common tools.

modules.name: Website
modules.oneLine: Where to see the kit, play the prototypes and follow the project.

items.title: The homepage
items.text: What Miniature Beasts is, how it plays step by step, the three devices, the latest screens and designs, and links to play and to the source.

items.title: The sandbox
items.text: Every prototype is published to the sandbox automatically after each change, with the build it is serving in the footer.

items.title: This roadmap
items.text: A public page showing what exists, what is being built and what comes next for each part of the project.

items.title: A real pitch with a playable demo
items.text: A fuller page built around the actual world and creatures, with a playable embedded in it.

items.title: Builder documentation
items.text: Guides for printing, wiring and assembling your own kit.

items.title: Devlog
items.text: Regular notes on what changed and why.

items.title: Kit sign-up
items.text: A way to hear when kits are ready.
